item.title: U.S. carries out new strikes on Iran after Trump threatened "a beating"
item.description: The U.S. carried out strikes on Iran on Wednesday night after President Trump earlier threatened the country with "a beating" following U.S. and Saudi Arabia's joint strikes on Iranian proxies in Iraq.

item.title: Blanche's nomination for AG on hold over fate of DOJ's "anti-weaponization fund"
item.description: Republican Sen. John Cornyn has demanded formal modifications to an agreement the Justice Department made with President Trump to settle his lawsuit against the IRS.

item.title: Dr. Anthony Fauci in October 2020 on COVID-19 | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: From October 2020, Dr. Jon LaPook's interview with Dr. Anthony Fauci about the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: K-pop group BTS won't submit music for 2027 Grammy Awards over new "Best Asian Pop" category
item.description: Maria Sherman, music reporter at the Associated Press, joins "The Daily Report" to break down what BTS' refusal to submit music for the 2027 Grammy Awards over a new category means as the band returns from an extended hiatus.

item.title: Acting CDC director says Fauci "abused the place of power" during pandemic
item.description: The acting director of the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention on Wednesday accused Dr. Anthony Fauci of an abuse of power during the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: Latest on Iran war after Saudi forces join U.S. strikes
item.description: Iran on Wednesday launched a barrage of missiles at American forces in the Middle East. This comes as the U.S. and Saudi Arabia strike Tehran-backed militias in Iraq. Ret. U.S. Navy Vice Adm. Robert Murrett joins with analysis.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial centers on ex's 911 call: "She killed the kids"
item.description: Prosecutors allege Lindsay Clancy made a "calculated decision" in killing her kids, while the defense says she was overmedicated and suffering from extreme postpartum psychosis.

item.title: Salman Rushdie attacker convicted in federal trial over 2022 stabbing
item.description: A man has been convicted of federal terrorism charges in the 2022 stabbing of author Salman Rushdie.

item.title: What drove the Dow to its worst day since April 2025?
item.description: Investors reacted sharply on Wednesday to the Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged amid persistent inflation and spikes in energy prices. Emily Russell, commentary and policy editor at Barron's, joins with analysis.

item.title: Legal analysis on whether Dr. Anthony Fauci can be punished for invoking Fifth Amendment
item.description: CBS News' legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down the legal implications of Dr. Anthony Fauci's invoking of the Fifth Amendment amid lawmakers' questions on the COVID-19 pandemic during Wednesday's Senate hearing.

item.title: Airport immigration arrests climb as result of increased ICE-TSA collaboration, sources say
item.description: Sources tell CBS News a recent rise in immigration-related arrests in U.S. airports is due to a closer collaboration between ICE and the TSA. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has the story.

item.title: Fauci invokes 5th in hearing, citing Rand Paul's "unhinged obsession"
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci appeared before the Senate to testify on the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic but invoked his Fifth Amendment rights in answering all questions.

item.title: Maps show where heavy rainfall poses flood risks across Northeast
item.description: The storm system that brought dangerous tornadoes to the Midwest earlier this week has now moved into New England, threatening to cause flooding in multiple states.

item.title: 2 firefighters die in Greece as others fight massive blaze in France
item.description: Two firefighters died in a blaze on the Greek island of Crete Wednesday while crews in France confronted a wildfire four times the size of Paris, officials said.

item.title: Extended Interview: NIH director Jay Bhattacharya on Fauci hearing, COVID-19 origins, more
item.description: Rob Gutman speaks with Jay Bhattacharya, director of the National Institutes of Health and acting director of the CDC, about Dr. Anthony Fauci's actions during the pandemic, the possible origins of COVID-19, vaccines and more.

item.title: Trump threatens to hit Iran "very hard" as conflicts expands
item.description: President Trump renewed his threats to hit Iran "very hard" on Wednesday following surprise attacks on U.S. forces in the Middle East. CBS News' chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Lawyer, 42, tries on a different suit, gives lifeguarding a try: "Best summer of my life"
item.description: Ben Schweer, a medical malpractice lawyer from Pittsburgh, tried on a different summer suit, becoming a lifeguard at Delaware's Rehoboth Beach. Mark Strassmann has the story.

item.title: 7/29: CBS Evening News
item.description: Parts of U.S. inundated by flash flooding and scorching temperatures; jurors in Clancy murder trial hear new testimony and evidence.

item.title: Rep. Debbie Dingell urges Michigan Democrats to unite regardless of who wins Senate primary
item.description: The closely-watched Democratic Senate primary in Michigan between Abdul El-Sayed and Haley Stevens is less than one week away. Democratic Rep. Debbie Dingell of Michigan joins "The Takeout" to weigh in on the divisions in the race.

item.title: What records reveal about Newsom's taxpayer-funded, California-branded free diaper program
item.description: CBS California Investigates reviewed 356 pages of state records behind California's $6.2 million diaper contract with Baby2Baby. Here is what they show.

item.title: Dr. Deborah Birx on combative Fauci hearing: "We have to have a better way forward than this"
item.description: Former White House Coronavirus Response Coordinator Dr. Deborah Birx worked, in her words, in the trenches with Dr. Anthony Fauci during the COVID-19 pandemic. Birx joins "The Takeout" with her thoughts on Fauci's diaries, his actions during the pandemic and the debate over COVID's origins.

item.title: Fed holds interest rates steady, but 3 officials vote for hike
item.description: Fed officials are leaving their benchmark rate unchanged for a fifth straight meeting, a sign they expect inflation to ease.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial jury hears ex-husband's 911 call after murders
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is standing trial on charges that she murdered her three young children in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in 2023.

item.title: Sen. Rand Paul says there's a "very real chance" Fauci could be prosecuted after contentious hearing
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment during a Senate hearing about the COVID-19 pandemic on Wednesday, angering Republican lawmakers. GOP Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky, who led the hearing, joins "The Takeout" with his reaction.

item.title: 7/29: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci invokes the Fifth Amendment in Senate hearing; Fed leaves interest rates unchanged.

item.title: Actor Jared Leto accused of criminal sexual conduct by 4 women
item.description: Four women say Hollywood star Jared Leto committed sexual crimes against them when they were teenagers, in interviews with the BBC.

item.title: Schools are testing pepper-spraying drones to stop shooters
item.description: Schools in three states will be equipped with drones this coming academic year that aim to find and deter active shooters within seconds.

item.title: U.S. says it thwarted Iranian missile attack on troops in Middle East
item.description: Iran launched multiple ballistic missiles at U.S. forces in the Middle East in what U.S. Central Command described as an "attempted surprise attack" on Tuesday.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy now on trial in murder of her 3 children in Massachusetts
item.description: Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing her three young children in her Duxbury, Massachusetts, home, is standing trial after opening statements were given Monday and testimony began.

item.title: Cyclospora boosts fears that deadlier foodborne outbreaks are ahead
item.description: Food safety experts say cuts to the public health system hobbled the response — and that the next outbreak could be much worse.
